samir: FYI we've got a cluster-wide MIG issue after the driver/CUDA bump to 537.23 / CUDA 12.2 on prod-east-2. Several nodes report MIG lockfile errors and their MIG configs are gone or show different UUIDs.

infra-bot: deploy-driver-job/2026-02-25 finished: driver=537.23, cuda=12.2, nodes touched=15, status=SUCCESS

maria: which nodes? any pods OOMing or GPU allocation failures?

samir: gpu-node-12, gpu-node-19, gpu-node-21. GPUs show up but `nvidia-smi` reports no MIG devices on those nodes. Example from gpu-node-12:

```bash
$ nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,gpu_uuid --format=csv
index, name, gpu_uuid
0, NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB, GPU-5c3a...b4d1
```

and

```bash
$ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-40GB (UUID: GPU-5c3a...b4d1)
No MIG devices found
```

jyoti: dmesg on gpu-node-19 shows:

```text
[  123.456789] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, pid=2345, GPU has fallen off the bus
[  123.457001] nvidia: module tainted: CKPT
[  123.457012] nvidia: mig-config-lock: failed to acquire lock: /var/lib/nvidia/mig-lock
```

oliver: this looks like nvidia-persistenced left a stale lock while the driver update replaced modules. Persistenced keeps MIG metadata in /var/lib/nvidia; after module swap the lock can prevent reapply. We saw similar with kernel-module rmmod ordering.

Suggested immediate runbook:
1) Drain affected node: `kubectl drain gpu-node-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data`.
2) Stop node GPU services: `systemctl stop kubelet && systemctl stop nvidia-persistenced`.
3) Verify no nvidia processes: `ps aux | grep -i nvidia`.
4) Remove stale lock and backup mig-config: `mv /var/lib/nvidia/mig-lock /var/lib/nvidia/mig-lock.bak` and `mv /var/lib/nvidia/mig-config.json /var/lib/nvidia/mig-config.json.bak`.
5) Recreate MIG profiles from saved spec (we keep per-node JSONs in s3://redwood-infra/mig-specs/) using the node-local tool: `s3-fetch /mig-specs/gpu-node-12.json && nvidia-smi mig -i 0 -c -g /path/to/spec.json` (note: adapt command as needed).
6) Start services: `systemctl start nvidia-persistenced && systemctl start kubelet` and uncordon.
If that fails, do a controlled reboot.

maria: can we automate steps 4-6 as a post-upgrade hook? this is blocking prod.

samir: I'll take ownership of rolling the three nodes now, starting with gpu-node-12. Will do one node at a time, verify pod reschedules and no scheduling failures. ETA ~ 30m.

jyoti: adding kernel/nvidia version checks to deploy job. I think the root cause is ordering: new driver modules loaded before persistenced restarted. Plan: change upgrade job to `systemctl stop nvidia-persistenced` before driver swap and `systemctl start` afterwards, plus post-check `nvidia-smi -L && nvidia-smi mig -L`.

infra-bot: scheduled rolling remediate job by samir for nodes [gpu-node-12, gpu-node-19, gpu-node-21] started at 1765554380

oliver: also add a check in monitor: compare MIG UUIDs pre/ post-upgrade and alert if mismatch; store pre-upgrade mig-config.json in job artifacts.

maria: ok noted. ping me in thread when first node is back.

samir: back in 22m — gpu-node-12 remediated, MIG profiles restored from spec, workloads back. continuing with gpu-node-19.

infra-bot: job progress: node gpu-node-12 = DONE, gpu-node-19 = IN_PROGRESS

jyoti: I'll prepare a quick RFC for changing the driver upgrade job to include persistenced stop + pre/post checks. rough patch ready.

maria: great. follow-up: create a short runbook in runbooks/ for on-call.

samir: will file a PR with the runbook after the rollout.

oliver: filing a postmortem doc after the incident with logs and timeline.
